chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Faith is not by adorning nor by wishing, but faith is what is sincere in the heart and confirmed by actions.
ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of faith (Iman) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Ibn Abi Umair, establishes the Shia doctrine of 'sincerity of the heart' (ikhlas) as the core of faith, distinguishing it from superficial verbalism. It underscores the inseparable link between internal conviction and external practice, a key theme in al-Saduq's theological framework. This definition aligns with the Shia understanding that true iman requires both knowledge and action, reflecting the holistic nature of belief.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from Hafs bin Bukhturi, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:
Faith is not by adorning nor by wishing, however, faith is what has been made sincere in the heart and creceded by actions.
